findings.finding: GET /health returns {"status":"ok"}; the frozen contract documents 200 {"status":"ok","database":"ok","version":"..."} and cites E15-S1-AC5. Two of three documented fields are absent.
findings.resolution: Human decision. api-contracts.md is frozen and out of scope for edits; either the contract line or the handler has to move. Omitting 'database' looks defensible (no database exists until group B) and omitting 'version' is defensible on disclosure grounds, which suggests the contract line is the thing that is wrong.

findings.finding: MoneyField uses a plain validator with no __get_pydantic_json_schema__, so OpenAPI generation raises PydanticInvalidForJsonSchema for any model that carries a money field. /openapi.json and /docs are 200 only because no route uses MoneyField yet; the first money-carrying contract breaks both.
findings.repro: class M(BaseModel): amount: MoneyField  ->  M.model_json_schema() raises

findings.finding: Redaction is opt-in by exact value registration inside a redact_values() scope. There is no pattern-based or key-name-based redaction, so any call site that logs applicant PII without registering the exact value leaks it verbatim (demonstrated). E15-S1-AC1 holds today only because the sole route logs no payload.
findings.mitigation_observed: tests/unit/test_log_redaction.py::test_modules_handling_applicant_pii_enter_a_redaction_scope is a structural guard on future call sites.

findings.finding: classify() and classify_by_days_past_due() live in the Config layer; E11-S1 Generation Contract operation 2 places the pure classifier in backend/src/types/delinquency.py, which at HEAD holds only the enum. No layering rule is broken (Config may import Types) but the owned-file contract in specs/bundles/E11-S1.json drifted.

AppError.context is serialized to the client verbatim with no allowlist, redaction or size limit, and 'error' is the exception class name. An internal path and a PAN placed in context by a caller were returned to the client in full. No production call site uses it yet (0 AppError subclasses), so this is a forward-looking outbound channel, but it is unguarded. Security-reviewer remit; recorded here with a live repro.

A caller-supplied X-Request-ID is accepted, echoed and logged with no length cap or character allowlist: a 5000-character id was reflected and logged in full. JSON escaping does prevent log-line forgery and header splitting was not reproducible, so the impact is log/header bloat rather than injection. Security-reviewer remit.

uvicorn.access is silenced (propagate=False, no handler) rather than routed through the JSON formatter. That is what closes the prior plain-text-access-line failure, but it discards uvicorn's access records (client address, bytes, protocol) and makes --access-log a no-op. The app's own truelend.access line replaces them and carries request_id. Also: the JSON formatter drops extra= fields entirely, so structured log context cannot be attached.
